questions.q: Why should the SSIS package and T-SQL DDL be committed to the portfolio repo as actual files, not just described?
options: GitHub requires every repo to contain at least one .sql file
Screenshots of code are not allowed on GitHub
SSIS packages cannot be described in a README under any circumstances
They're readable directly on GitHub, letting a reviewer see your real ETL logic and schema decisions without installing anything
questions.explain: Committing the real .dtsx and .sql files as text lets a reviewer verify your resume's claims directly, in minutes, without needing SQL Server or SSIS installed.

questions.q: Why do the SSRS report and Power BI dashboard need screenshots or a recording, unlike the SSIS package and SQL files?
options: Because SSRS and Power BI don't produce any visual output worth showing
Because .rdl and .pbix files aren't viewable in a browser the way code is — screenshots and a recording are what let a reviewer see the finished product
Because screenshots are required by GitHub's terms of service
Because .rdl and .pbix files are always corrupted when uploaded to GitHub
questions.explain: Report and dashboard files are opaque without the tool installed, so screenshots and a short recording substitute for a reviewer clicking through them live.

questions.q: What is the most common mistake this lesson identifies when talking through a project in a portfolio review?
options: Talking for too short a time about the project
Not mentioning Power BI at all during the review
Bringing printed screenshots to the review
Opening with a tour of the tool list instead of the business problem the project solves
questions.explain: Leading with tools answers a question nobody asked. Leading with the business problem answers the question a reviewer actually cares about: can you solve a real problem with these tools?

questions.q: What four things does this lesson say a README should cover, in order?
options: The author's resume, their contact information, their availability, and their salary expectations
The business problem, the architecture, the design decisions worth explaining, and what it looks like (screenshots)
A list of every file in the repository with no further explanation
A history of every course in the Microsoft Data & BI Developer program
questions.explain: That order does the work of connecting the files together for the reviewer, instead of leaving them to reverse-engineer how the pieces fit.

questions.q: According to this lesson, what should a short recorded walkthrough of the project focus on?
options: A ten-minute recording of every click made while building the SSIS package
Reading the README aloud word for word with no screen recording
A concise 2-3 minute narration opening on the business problem and showing the finished report and dashboard
Only the SQL Server installation process
questions.explain: A long click-by-click recording gets skipped. A short, focused recording that mirrors the business-problem-first talk-through gets watched.
